verdicts.summary: The modelCatalogOnly branch returns early and calls only refreshModelCatalog. Failures are swallowed, and the empty providers list is never recorded.
verdicts.scenario: I tried three cases. (1) An older server: the client checks the modelCatalogRefresh capability first. (2) A fetch failure: it is caught by Effect.catchCause at ModelManifest.ts:250, and the registry wraps the rest in recoverRefreshFailure. (3) The empty `{providers: []}` result: onSuccess returns early at server.ts:1423 when instanceId or cwd is undefined, so the empty list is never recorded. The singleFlight key includes modelCatalogOnly, so this call does not merge with a full refresh.

verdicts.summary: The two-pass loop covers the case where an in-flight pass started before the fetch. Each pass reads updatedAt at its start and records it only after the pass succeeds.
verdicts.scenario: I tried an in-flight refreshAll that started before the fetch. The picker call joins it through the shared Deferred, and the pass records the older updatedAt. The loop then runs a second pass, which starts after the first one clears the in-flight ref and reads the new updatedAt. I also tried a failed pass: the Ref.set at line 666 is skipped, and refreshAll() fails and is caught by recoverRefreshFailure. A stale CDN manifest is rejected at ModelManifest.ts:253, so updatedAt never goes backwards. One small gap remains. Per-provider probe failures inside refreshOneSource may not fail the pass, so the ref can advance even though one provider was not re-probed. I did not open refreshOneSource to confirm.
